DEVELOPER HANDOFF
v1.0

Reputation Engine - Technical Specification

Multi-tenant NFC tap-to-review platform with server-side routing, sentiment triage, reseller commissions, and Stripe subscriptions. Built to be assembled quickly with AI coding tools.

1. Core architectural principle

Write each card once. Control everything server-side. Every NFC card is encoded a single time with a permanent URL containing an unguessable id: https://app.DOMAIN.com/t/{cardId}. The card is never re-encoded. When tapped, the server resolves cardId → business → current settings and decides where to send the visitor. "Activating" or re-pointing a card is a database update, not physical access. This is what makes fulfillment instant and the system scalable.

Tap request flow

GET /t/:cardId
  1. Look up card. If unassigned/disabled -> generic fallback page.
  2. Load business + brand + review_url + subscription flags.
  3. Render branded rating page (server-rendered, fast, edge-friendly).
  4. Visitor selects 1-5 stars (client POSTs to /api/tap).
     - 4-5: record tap, 302 redirect to business.review_url
     - 1-3: record tap, show private feedback form (public link ALSO shown = compliant)
  5. On feedback submit -> store + fire SMS (Twilio) + email (Resend) to owner.
Compliance requirement (non-negotiable in code): the low-rating branch must still surface the public review link. Do not hard-gate. Enforce "feedback-first, not review-blocking" at the component level so no reseller/business config can turn it into review gating (Google/Yelp/FTC violation).

2. Recommended stack

Chosen for speed of AI-assisted build, low run cost, and fast edge redirects. Swap equivalents freely; the architecture is stack-agnostic.

Framework
Next.js (App Router) - one codebase for marketing site, dashboards, tap pages, and API routes. (Alt: Lovable/React if building visually with AI.)
DB + Auth
Supabase (Postgres) - Row-Level Security for multi-tenant isolation, built-in auth, roles. (Alt: Postgres + Clerk/Auth.js.)
Hosting
Vercel or Cloudflare Pages/Workers. The /t/:cardId resolver should run at the edge for low-latency taps.
Payments
Stripe - subscriptions ($15/mo), card-order checkout, reseller payouts via Stripe Connect (optional).
SMS
Twilio - instant low-rating alert to owner/manager.
Email
Resend - alerts, order confirmations, activation notices.
NFC write
NTAG213 chips + "NFC Tools" app (or bulk pre-encoding by supplier via CSV of URLs).

3. Roles & tenancy

RoleCan do
Super Admin (us)Everything: manage resellers, businesses, card inventory/batches, fulfillment, billing, payouts, global analytics.
Reseller (rep)Self-signup. Buy cards at wholesale, assign/activate cards to businesses, view own sales + commission ledger + payouts.
Business (client)Set review destination URL, customize landing page (logo/colors/copy), read feedback inbox + star analytics, manage $15/mo subscription.

Enforce isolation with Postgres RLS: a business row is readable only by its owner + assigned reseller + admin. Never rely on client-side checks alone.

4. Data model (minimum viable schema)

users        (id, email, role[admin|reseller|business], stripe_customer_id, created_at)
resellers    (id, user_id→users, display_name, commission_rate, payout_method, status)
businesses   (id, name, logo_url, brand_color, review_url, review_platform,
              owner_phone, owner_email, reseller_id→resellers,
              subscription_status[none|active|past_due|canceled],
              stripe_subscription_id, created_at)
cards        (id // the unguessable cardId in the URL, e.g. 12+ char base62,
              business_id→businesses nullable until assigned,
              status[unassigned|active|disabled], batch_id, activated_at)
taps         (id, card_id→cards, rating[1-5], redirected_to, user_agent, created_at)
feedback     (id, business_id→businesses, rating, customer_name, customer_phone,
              message, resolved[bool], created_at)
commissions  (id, reseller_id, business_id, stripe_invoice_id,
              type[card_sale|sub_month_1|sub_month_2], amount,
              status[pending|paid|reversed], created_at)
card_batches (id, quantity, printed[bool], notes, created_at)

cardId must be random and unguessable (e.g. 12-char nanoid), never sequential - otherwise the URL space can be walked to hijack or enumerate cards.

5. Key API endpoints

RoutePurpose
GET /t/:cardIdPublic. Resolve card, render branded rating page. Edge-cached per card where possible.
POST /api/tapPublic. Record rating; return redirect target (4-5) or feedback-form flag (1-3).
POST /api/feedbackPublic. Store private feedback; trigger Twilio SMS + Resend email to owner.
POST /api/cards/assignReseller/admin. Bind a card to a business and set status=active.
POST /api/checkout/cardsReseller. Stripe Checkout for wholesale card orders.
POST /api/checkout/subscriptionBusiness. Stripe Checkout for $15/mo reputation subscription.
POST /api/webhooks/stripeStripe events. Drives activation + commission ledger (see §6).
GET /api/business/feedbackBusiness. Paginated feedback inbox + analytics.

6. Payments & commission logic (Stripe webhooks)

All money automation is webhook-driven so nothing is manual.

Stripe eventAction
checkout.session.completed (subscription)Mark business subscription_status=active. If the card is unassigned/inactive, auto-activate it now (card goes live the moment payment clears).
invoice.paidCount paid invoices on this subscription. 1st paid invoice → write commissions(sub_month_1, $15) to the reseller. 2nd → sub_month_2, $15. 3rd+ → no commission (100% company).
charge.refunded / invoice.payment_failedIf it matches a rep-credited invoice, set that commission status=reversed (clawback). Prevents gaming with signup-then-cancel.
customer.subscription.deletedSet subscription_status=canceled. Card can revert to a generic review link or stay pointed (business decision).
Anchor commissions to successful paid invoices, not calendar months or signup date. This handles retries, failed cards, and re-subscribes correctly, and pairs with the refund clawback so reps are only paid on money actually kept.

7. NFC card production

  • Chip: NTAG213 is sufficient (URL fits easily). ~$2/card at low volume, less in bulk.
  • Encoding: a single NDEF URI record = https://app.DOMAIN.com/t/{cardId}. Free "NFC Tools" app writes one in ~5 seconds; lock the tag to read-only after writing.
  • At volume: pre-generate a batch of cardIds (status unassigned), export a CSV of URLs, and either (a) write them in-house or (b) hand the CSV to an NFC printing vendor for pre-encoding + custom print.
  • Assignment to a business happens later in software, so generic stock can be produced ahead of demand.

8. Security checklist

  • Unguessable cardId (nanoid 12+); rate-limit /api/tap and /api/feedback to stop spam/skew.
  • Postgres RLS for every tenant table; server-side authorization on all dashboard mutations.
  • Verify Stripe webhook signatures; make webhook handlers idempotent (dedupe on event id).
  • Store only what you need from customers (name + phone are optional on feedback); post a privacy notice.
  • Bot/abuse protection on public tap pages; cap taps per card per short window.
  • PII (owner phone/email) encrypted at rest via provider defaults; least-privilege API keys per integration.

9. Build phases

PhaseScope
PHASE 1 Prove the mechanicTap resolver, branded rating page, 4-5 vs 1-3 split, private feedback form, Twilio SMS + Resend email alert. One hardcoded demo business. Goal: a card you can tap live in front of an owner.
PHASE 2 Make it a productAuth + roles, business dashboard (review URL, page customization, feedback inbox, analytics), card assignment/activation.
PHASE 3 The business enginePublic marketing site + reseller self-signup, Stripe card checkout + $15/mo subscriptions, commission ledger + reseller dashboard, super-admin panel + fulfillment, batch/inventory tooling.

11. Extensibility (design for the endgame)

The platform is a lead-generation engine for higher-ticket website + AI services. Build the business dashboard with room for upsell modules and clean contact capture, so services can be cross-sold to accounts that already pay and trust the product. Keep businesses records rich (industry, contact, engagement) for later segmentation.
